# Voxelization

Also called: Voxel generation, Grid discretization, Digitization

## Overview
Voxelization is the process of mapping a continuous conceptual or physical source (such as a triangle mesh, point cloud, or parametric surface) into a discrete volumetric representation suitable for rendering or simulation. It solves the problem of converting unstructured or continuous geometry into a structured grid of volume elements (voxels) that can be efficiently accessed by downstream pipelines like ray marching or sparse octree construction. It differs from [Procedural and implicit volumes](13-procedural-and-implicit-volumes.md) by explicitly generating a discrete data structure rather than evaluating an analytic function on-the-fly, and from [Acquisition](14-acquisition.md) by being a deterministic geometric conversion step rather than a sensor-based reconstruction process.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family map a conceptual or physical source into a discrete or analytic volumetric representation suitable for rendering. The core mechanism involves:
1.  **Domain Definition**: Establishing a spatial domain, typically a 3D grid with resolution $(N_x, N_y, N_z)$ and bounding box, or an infinite analytic space [S1][S3, unofficial].
2.  **Value Assignment**: Determining the value (density, distance, color) for each point in the domain based on the source method (geometric intersection, function evaluation, or physical state) [S1, S12].
3.  **Storage/Access**: Either storing the result in a discrete array (voxelization, simulation) or providing an interface to compute it on-the-fly (procedural) [S1][S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md)
Converts a continuous triangle mesh into a discrete volumetric representation by projecting the mesh geometry onto a 3D grid using rasterization primitives. It solves the problem of generating a voxelized surface or volume from polygonal data without performing explicit ray-triangle intersection tests for every voxel. It differs from [Voxel Carving](1213-voxel-carving.md) by using constructive rasterization rather than destructive projection, and from [Analytic and Algebraic Methods](7913-analytic-and-algebraic-methods.md) by relying on discrete sampling of rasterized fragments rather than solving geometric equations. Choose this method for high-performance GPU-based mesh voxelization where explicit geometric intersection is too costly.

### [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md)
Converts a discrete set of 3D points into a structured voxel grid, mapping continuous world-space coordinates to discrete integer grid indices. It solves the problem of organizing unstructured point data into a regular grid suitable for downstream volume rendering, sparse voxel octree construction, or neural network processing. Unlike [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) which projects geometry to screen space, this method operates directly in world space. It differs from [Hard Voxelization](5345-hard-voxelization.md) by explicitly handling feature aggregation and sparse data structures, and from [Point Cloud to Gaussian Converter](1788-point-cloud-to-gaussian-converter.md) by producing discrete grid cells rather than continuous density fields. Choose this method when the input is already a point cloud and feature aggregation (mean, sum) is required.

### [VoxelGrid from Mesh (Fill Method)](1013-voxelgrid-from-mesh-fill-method.md)
Produces a voxel grid from a mesh by first computing the surface occupancy and then filling the interior holes using morphological operations. It differs from [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) and [Conservative Voxelization](3247-conservative-voxelization.md) by relying on binary morphological closing rather than geometric intersection tests or rasterization coverage to determine interior voxels. It is distinct from [Interior Voxelize](995-interior-voxelize.md) in that it explicitly uses a two-step process of surface extraction followed by dilation/filling. Choose this method when a watertight solid volume is required from a potentially non-watertight or sparse surface mesh.

### [Voxel Grid Data Generation Pipeline](1208-voxel-grid-data-generation-pipeline.md)
Generates labeled 3D voxel grids from sequential scan data, specifically designed to handle occlusions and temporal consistency between prior and current observations. It differs from standard voxelization by maintaining two distinct grid states (prior and past) and explicitly updating occlusion masks based on camera pose transformations, ensuring that newly observed geometry correctly occludes previous estimates. It builds on [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) by adding a temporal, scan-based processing loop. Choose this method for SLAM or dynamic scene reconstruction where temporal consistency and occlusion handling are critical.

### [Voxel Carving](1213-voxel-carving.md)
Reconstructs a dense, filled 3D voxel grid from a set of 2D depth maps or silhouettes captured from multiple camera viewpoints. Unlike surface-only voxelization methods that mark only boundary voxels, carving creates a volumetric representation of the object's interior. It differs from [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by explicitly enforcing consistency across multiple views to fill the volume, rather than projecting mesh geometry directly into a grid. Choose this method for multi-view stereo reconstruction from depth sensors or images.

### [Coordinate Grid Generation](1273-coordinate-grid-generation.md)
Produces a structured set of spatial coordinates (typically in Normalized Device Coordinates, NDC, range $[-1, 1]$) that align with the discrete sampling grid of a volume or image. It solves the problem of mapping integer pixel or voxel indices to continuous physical or normalized space for neural field training, ray casting, and SDF evaluation. It differs from its sibling [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by generating the *sample points* themselves rather than determining *which* voxels a primitive occupies, and from [3D Coordinate Grid Generation](2333-3d-coordinate-grid-generation.md) by primarily targeting 2D image-plane coordinates for ray origin generation, though it extends to 3D. Choose this method when preparing input tensors for neural networks or ray marching shaders.

### [Voxel Occupancy Test](1281-voxel-occupancy-test.md)
Determines whether a given set of continuous world-space points lies within any occupied voxel of a pre-computed voxel grid. It solves the problem of spatial querying for point clouds or particle systems against a discrete volumetric representation, returning a boolean mask indicating inclusion. Unlike [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) which projects geometry to determine occupancy, this method performs a direct lookup against an existing grid structure, serving as the inverse operation of voxel generation. Choose this method for collision detection or particle filtering against a static voxel environment.

### [3D Scan-conversion](1895-3d-scan-conversion.md)
Converts geometric primitives (polygons) into a volumetric dataset, combines them with existing volumetric data using volume matting operators, and renders the resulting composite ensemble using standard volume rendering techniques. It sets itself apart from hybrid ray tracing by pre-filtering and sampling geometry into the voxel grid, allowing the use of standard ray-casting for the final image while avoiding aliasing artifacts through analytic anti-aliasing. Choose this method when mixing explicit geometry with volumetric data in a single rendering pass.

### [Virtual Voxel](1987-virtual-voxel.md)
A rasterization-based voxel renderer designed for the real-time visualization and modification of large-scale voxel scenes (e.g., $4^{12}$ resolution) by combining virtual texture and virtual geometry concepts. It streams appropriate levels of detail into GPU memory using a two-level data structure, storing data linearly to enable efficient real-time editing (Union/Subtraction). Unlike previous graph-based voxel visualization methods, it employs a rasterization rendering pipeline, resulting in highly efficient modification of large scenes. Choose this method for interactive voxel editors or large-scale voxel-based games.

### [Voxelization of Lines and Planes](2472-voxelization-of-lines-and-planes.md)
Generates a discrete, topologically correct representation of 2D lines and 3D planes (and by extension, polygon meshes) that is both **N-separating** and **N-minimal**. It solves the problem of "holes" in voxelized surfaces where a connected ray path could penetrate the original continuous surface without intersecting any voxel. Unlike standard rasterization which may produce gaps, this method uses a geometric slab defined by the surface normal and grid resolution to guarantee that no N-connected path (6-connected or 26-connected) can pass through the discretization without hitting a voxel. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by providing formal topological proofs of separability and minimality rather than relying on heuristic coverage. Choose this method when topological correctness (no leaks) is required for ray marching or fluid simulation.

### [Relaxed Connectivity Voxelization](2481-relaxed-connectivity-voxelization.md)
A method for voxelizing effectively one-dimensional input (1D, 2D, or 3D primitives) in 3D space that ensures the resulting voxels form a connected path, preventing gaps in flow simulation or fill operations. It produces a 26-connected path, allowing for fewer voxels than 6-connected methods while still maintaining connectivity. Unlike existing algorithms restricted to 1D primitives (e.g., line segments), this method works for input composed of 2D or 3D primitives that are effectively 1D. Choose this method for voxelizing curves, skeletons, or thin structures where connectivity is paramount.

### [Mesh-to-Voxel Geometry Shader](2800-mesh-to-voxel-geometry-shader.md)
A real-time DirectX technique that converts mesh objects into voxel-like cubes by iterating over integer grid positions within a triangle's bounding box and emitting explicit cube geometry for grid cells close to the triangle plane. Unlike rasterization-based voxelization which fills pixels or conservative voxelization which determines occupancy, this method explicitly generates the 3D geometry of every intersecting voxel, resulting in significantly higher vertex and triangle counts. Choose this method when the output must be standard triangle geometry for further rasterization or physics processing.

### [Grid Resolution Calculation](2908-grid-resolution-calculation.md)
Determines the discrete dimensions $(N_x, N_y, N_z)$ of a uniform 3D voxel grid based on the continuous extent of the scene's bounding box and a target density or aspect ratio constraint. It solves the problem of mapping a continuous world-space volume to a fixed-size integer array while preserving the geometric aspect ratio of the input. It differs from adaptive methods by producing a single global resolution for the entire grid, and from fixed-resolution approaches by scaling dynamically with the scene's bounding box dimensions. Choose this method as a preprocessing step to define grid parameters for other voxelization methods.

### [Conservative Voxelization](3247-conservative-voxelization.md)
A hardware-accelerated algorithm for polygonal models that guarantees conservative correctness: every voxel intersecting the input model is correctly recognized, solving the problem where previous approaches miss intersecting voxels. It differs from standard rasterization-based voxelization by computing the exact depth range of the intersection between the triangle and the voxel column, rather than using a single depth value (e.g., the fragment center) which leads to missed voxels. Choose this method when missing even a single intersecting voxel causes errors in downstream volume rendering or collision detection.

### [View-Adaptive Voxelization](3313-view-adaptive-voxelization.md)
A GPU-friendly, real-time technique for rendering homogeneous media defined by particles (e.g., SPH fluids) by computing view-adaptive binary voxelizations with on-the-fly compression. It solves the problem of high-resolution volumetric data exceeding available GPU memory by adapting the voxel grid to the viewport and using a span-based surface representation. Unlike sibling methods that may require preprocessing (such as scalar field conversion or mesh generation) or target out-of-core rendering with significant setup times, this method directly processes unsorted particle data to achieve interactive speeds. It sets itself apart by constructing a perspective voxel grid at full render resolution, typically using ~16,000 depth layers, and compressing it into surface spans for efficient translucency and refraction rendering. Choose this method for real-time particle-based fluid rendering.

### [Mesh to Voxel Generation via AABB-Triangle Intersection](3775-mesh-to-voxel-generation-via-aabb-triangle-intersection.md)
Converts a 3D triangle mesh into a solid voxel model by first identifying surface voxels through Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) vs. Triangle intersection tests, and then filling the interior volume using a scanline fill algorithm. It differs from rasterization-based voxelization by operating directly in world space with geometric intersection tests rather than projecting geometry onto a screen, and from point cloud voxelization by explicitly handling surface topology to ensure watertight interiors. Choose this method for CPU-based, robust mesh voxelization where topological correctness is required.

### [Voxel Grid Optimization](4131-voxel-grid-optimization.md)
Encompasses post-generation techniques applied to discrete 3D voxel grids to improve data quality, reduce storage requirements, or accelerate downstream rendering and processing pipelines. Unlike sibling methods in [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) that focus on the geometric conversion of primitives into voxels, this family addresses the properties of the resulting grid itself. It distinguishes itself by operating on the *data* rather than the *geometry*, offering solutions for noise reduction ([3D Voxel Grid Smoothing](833-3d-voxel-grid-smoothing.md)), compression ([Binary Voxel RLE Encoding](1071-binary-voxel-rle-encoding.md)), structural simplification ([Occupancy Voxel Creation](2628-occupancy-voxel-creation.md)), and access pattern efficiency ([Bounding Volume Optimization](3583-bounding-volume-optimization.md)). Choose this method after initial voxelization to prepare data for storage or efficient traversal.

### [Voronoi-like Segmentation Volume Generation](4218-voronoi-like-segmentation-volume-generation.md)
Creates a 3D volume where each voxel is assigned a label corresponding to the index of its nearest neighbor in a synthetic, Poisson-distributed point set. It solves the problem of generating structured, spatially coherent segmentation labels for volume data without relying on input geometry, effectively creating a "Voronoi-like" partitioning of space. Unlike [Soft Voronoi Decomposition](7634-soft-voronoi-decomposition.md), which produces differentiable, soft boundaries for gradient-based optimization, this method produces hard, discrete segmentations suitable for texture synthesis or parameter initialization. Choose this method for generating synthetic training data or spatial partitioning labels.

### [Sparse and Hierarchical Structures](4391-sparse-and-hierarchical-structures.md)
Addresses the memory and computational inefficiency of dense, uniform voxel grids by storing only occupied regions using hierarchical data structures (typically octrees) or sparse hash maps. It solves the problem of rendering or processing large-scale 3D scenes or high-resolution volumetric data that exceed available main memory or require adaptive resolution. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) and [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md) by focusing on the *storage and traversal* of the voxelized data in a hierarchical manner, rather than just the initial conversion from primitives to voxels. Choose this method for large-scale scenes or high-resolution data where memory efficiency is critical.

### [Voxel Coloring](4418-voxel-coloring.md)
A volumetric reconstruction algorithm that uses color consistency across multiple views to distinguish object surface voxels from background. It solves the problem of 3D shape recovery from uncalibrated or calibrated multi-view images by starting with a fully opaque volume and iteratively carving away voxels that exhibit inconsistent colors across input images. Unlike Space Carving, which requires multiple scans and arbitrary camera placement, Voxel Coloring relies on an ordinal visibility constraint to allow reconstruction in a single monotonic scan, simplifying visibility handling at the cost of restricting camera placement. Choose this method for multi-view stereo reconstruction from color images.

### [Parametric Surface Voxelization](6032-parametric-surface-voxelization.md)
Converts continuous parametric surfaces (such as NURBS or subdivision patches) into a discrete voxel grid by treating the 2D parameter domain as a point cloud. It differs from standard mesh voxelization by operating directly on the parametric definition rather than a triangulated approximation, allowing for the handling of complex implicit or free-form surfaces. Unlike rasterization-based methods that project 3D geometry to screen space, this method projects the 2D parameter space into 3D world space and then to the voxel grid, leveraging the vertex shader for coordinate transformation. Choose this method for voxelizing NURBS, subdivision surfaces, or implicit functions.

### [Volumetric Attribute and Density Formation](6304-volumetric-attribute-and-density-formation.md)
Defines the mechanism for populating the discrete voxel grid indices produced by [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) with continuous physical properties such as density, color, opacity, and directional normals. While the parent family determines *which* voxels are occupied, this family determines *what* those voxels contain. It differs from sibling methods like [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) or [Interior Voxelize](995-interior-voxelize.md) by focusing on the semantic content (attributes) and statistical aggregation (density) of the voxel data rather than the geometric intersection logic itself. Choose this method when assigning physical properties to voxelized geometry.

### [Mesh Voxelization](6514-mesh-voxelization.md)
Converts a continuous triangular surface mesh (e.g., STL, OBJ) into a discrete 3D voxel grid by determining the occupancy of each grid cell via ray-mesh intersection tests. Unlike [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md), which projects geometry onto a 2D plane and extrudes coverage, this method evaluates the topological relationship (inside/outside) of the voxel center relative to the closed surface using the ray casting parity rule. It serves as the foundational technique for generating solid or surface-only voxel representations from polygonal models, distinct from [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md) which operates on discrete samples rather than continuous geometry. Choose this method for robust, CPU-based solid mesh voxelization.

### [GPU and Parallel Acceleration Voxelization](6878-gpu-and-parallel-acceleration-voxelization.md)
Encompasses methods that accelerate the conversion of continuous primitives (meshes, points, or parametric curves) into discrete voxel grids by leveraging the massive parallelism of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Unlike CPU-based approaches, these methods typically map individual voxels or primitives to parallel threads to compute occupancy, distance, or geometric attributes simultaneously. They are distinguished from their siblings by their reliance on GPU-specific execution models (such as CUDA kernels or OpenGL compute shaders) to handle the high computational cost of spatial intersection tests and attribute accumulation. Choose this method for high-throughput voxelization of large datasets.

### [Voxel Format Generation](6914-voxel-format-generation.md)
Converts 3D Gaussian Splats into a sparse voxel octree for collision detection, outputting metadata (.voxel.json) and binary data (.voxel.bin), optionally generating a .collision.glb mesh. Choose this method when converting Gaussian Splatting representations into a format suitable for collision detection or traditional rendering engines.

### [3D Gaussian Voxelization](7020-3d-gaussian-voxelization.md)
Converts a set of 3D Gaussians into a set of unique voxels and their associated features for efficient processing by a 3D network. Choose this method when preparing Gaussian Splatting data for neural network processing or sparse voxel storage.

### [Specific Data Formats and Primitives](7148-specific-data-formats-and-primitives.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Solid Volume Accumulation via Sphere-Box Intersection](7681-solid-volume-accumulation-via-sphere-box-intersection.md)
Iterates over points and their bounding voxels, accumulating the sphere-box intersection volume into a dense NumPy array indexed by compact voxel linear index. Choose this method for voxelizing sphere-based particle systems or soft bodies where volumetric overlap needs to be accumulated.

### [Analytic and Algebraic Methods](7913-analytic-and-algebraic-methods.md)
Converts continuous geometric primitives (meshes, points, or parametric surfaces) into discrete volumetric grids by evaluating exact geometric intersections or integrals against voxel cells, rather than relying on screen-space rasterization or stochastic sampling. This family solves the problem of aliasing and discretization errors inherent in projection-based methods, providing high-fidelity, often differentiable, volumetric representations. It sets itself apart from [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by avoiding projection artifacts and from [Monte Carlo 2D Voxelization](1734-monte-carlo-voxelization.md) by using deterministic geometric evaluation. Choose this method when high accuracy and differentiability are required.

### [Template-based Voxelization](7964-template-based-voxelization.md)
A class for computing the digitization of a triangle or a Mesh. It determines if a voxel belongs to the digitization based on whether a template centered at the voxel intersects the triangle. Choose this method for template-based geometric digitization.

### [Mesh Topology and Robust Digitization](8496-mesh-topology-and-robust-digitization.md)
Not given in the sources.

### Recursive Voxelization with Interval Arithmetic
Rendering of recursively voxelized object space with interval arithmetic [S5, unofficial].

### Low-Detail Obstacle Voxelization
Using simplified meshes for obstacles to allow voxelization at every frame with little performance cost [S6, unofficial].
*   **Parameter**: Mesh LOD: Use a low level of detail mesh for each obstacle [S6, unofficial].

### Distance-based Voxelization
A method to voxelize objects directly without polygon conversion by including voxels where the distance to the surface S is smaller than a threshold t [S7].
*   **Steps**: Scan a subset of the voxel space in the vicinity of the surface S, efficiently measure the distance to surface S for each voxel, and generate a 6- or 26-separating representation [S7]. For general surfaces, use the Lagrangian Method to find the point on the surface minimizing the distance to a random 3D point [S7].
*   **Formula**: The distance minimization problem is defined by minimizing the squared Euclidean distance function: $p(x, y, z) = (x - x_0)^2 + (y - y_0)^2 + (z - z_0)^2$, where $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$ is a point on the surface and $(x, y, z)$ is the voxel center [S7].
*   **Parameters**: Sphere radius: 61.4. Cylinder radius: 49.7 and height: 158.2. Function parameter k for $x^2 + y^2 + kz = 0$: 10.0 [S7].
*   **Pitfall**: Solutions via the Lagrangian Method may require solving high-order polynomial equations without analytical solutions; numerical methods must be used for high accuracy [S7].
*   **Comparison**: For regular shapes like spheres and cylinders, distance measurement is straightforward; for general surfaces, the Lagrangian Method is required [S7].

### Displacement Voxelization
An extension to the base framework that uses PN-triangles and displacement mapping to voxelize low-resolution meshes with rugged surfaces at high resolution, achieving visual quality comparable to conventional voxelization of high-resolution meshes [S8, unofficial].
*   **Steps**: Perform triangle subdivision using the hardware tessellator as in the base method. Use PN-triangles to reconstruct mesh details. Utilize the positions and normals of the PN-triangles to apply displacement mapping during the voxelization process [S8, unofficial].

### Asynchronous Voxel Update
Updating the voxel world at a lower frequency than the render frame rate to leverage temporal coherency of static or slow-moving light sources and dynamic models [S9, unofficial].
*   **Parameter**: Update frequency: The voxelization can be performed at a lower frequency, such as every 5 frames [S9, unofficial].
*   **Pitfall**: Lower update frequency causes the voxel model to lag behind the triangle mesh, resulting in visual artifacts [S9, unofficial].

### Voxelization Engine Workload Distribution
A pipeline architecture distributing voxelization tasks between CPU and GPU to handle ROI computation, classification, and rasterization efficiently [S10, unofficial].
*   **Steps**: CPU: Compute Region of Interest (ROI) by updating index buffer dynamically. Perform normal-based classification and bucket sorting for polygonal models. Transfer updated data through AGP port. GPU: Rasterize classified primitives in streaming mode. Encode and store results as 2D textures in three directional sheet buffers. Create proxy rectangles to texture map patches for rendering/access [S10, unofficial].

### Local Voxelization
Voxelize a mesh in the region of a cube around a specific point, rather than globally. Useful to reduce memory cost for small values of pitch as opposed to global voxelization [S1].
*   **Parameters**: mesh: Source geometry, type trimesh.Trimesh. point: Point in space to voxelize around, shape (3,) float. pitch: Side length of a single voxel cube. radius: Number of voxel cubes to return in each direction. fill: Boolean, default True. When True, uses proximity.contains to fill the resulting voxels [S1].
*   **Layout**: Return type: VoxelGrid instance with resolution (m, m, m) where m=2*radius+1 [S1].
*   **Code**: `local_voxelize(mesh, point: ArrayLike, pitch: float | floating | int | integer, radius: float | floating | int | integer, fill: bool = True, **kwargs) → VoxelGrid | None` [S1].
*   **Pitfall**: When fill=True, the method uses proximity.contains to fill voxels, which may be meaningless for non-watertight meshes [S1].

### 3D Scan-Conversion for Geometric/Volumetric Mixing
*   **Steps**: Bandlimit the object to the Nyquist frequency in all three dimensions. Sample the object in a manner that limits losses due to quantization. Use volume rendering's partial opacity capability to handle the resulting voxel representation and avoid aliasing artifacts common in binary voxel representations [S11, unofficial].

### Fine-tuning with Differentiable Quantization
An optimization step to mitigate quality loss from quantization (texture seams, aliasing) by fine-tuning extracted assets using pseudo ground truth and differentiable quantization [S12].
*   **Steps**: Fix mesh geometry and use rendered normal and texture images from the mesh optimization stage as pseudo ground truth references. Optimize using pixel-wise MSE loss and VGG perceptual loss. Use a differentiable quantization module that gives quantized values in the forward pass and keeps gradients untouched in the backward pass. Store mesh as Draco-compressed .obj file; other assets (normal map, texture maps, volume data in hash table, offset table) as PNG files [S12].
*   **Layout**: Occupancy Image: Stores occupancy of the N^3 grid as an image where each voxel's occupancy status corresponds to a single bit [S12].

## Background
Voxelization originated as a fundamental technique in volume visualization and computer graphics to bridge the gap between continuous geometric representations (polygons, implicit surfaces) and discrete volumetric data structures. Early work focused on scan-conversion algorithms for linear and quadratic objects [S1][S11, unofficial]. The method has evolved to support various input types, including triangle meshes [S1][S4, unofficial][S7][S8, S10, unofficial], point clouds [S4, S5, unofficial], and parametric surfaces [S1][S2, unofficial]. Modern applications include real-time global illumination via voxel cone tracing [S2, S9, unofficial], fluid simulation [S6, unofficial], and neural rendering [S5, unofficial][S12]. The family has expanded to include GPU-accelerated methods [S4, S6, S8, S10, unofficial], conservative voxelization for correctness [S1], and topological guarantees for separability [S2, unofficial][S7].
